Let us now assume that for a particular value of $n$
$$\begin{aligned}
Y_{n}=A_{n .0} \Sigma\left(\mu^{n}\right) & +A_{n .1} \Sigma\left(\mu^{n-2} \lambda^{1}\right)+\text { \&c. } \\
& +A_{n .,} \Sigma\left(\mu^{n-2} \lambda^{n}\right)+\text { \&c. }
\end{aligned}$$
(34)
where the $A$ 's are numerical coefficients. We may write the
series in the abbreviated form
$$Y_{n}=S\left[A_{n \cdot n} \Sigma\left(\mu^{n-2 s} \lambda^{s}\right)\right],$$
(35)
where $S$ indicates a summation in which all values of 8 , including
zero, not greater than $\frac{1}{2} n$, are to be taken.
To obtain the corresponding solid harmonic of negative degree
$(n+1)$ and order $n$, we multiply by $r^{-(n+1)}$, and obtain
$$V_{n}=S\left[A_{n . s} r^{2 .-2 n-1} \Sigma\left(p^{n-2 s} \lambda^{*}\right)\right]$$
(36)
putting $r \mu=p$, as in equation (3).
If we differentiate $V_{n}$ with respect to a new axis $h_{m}$ we obtain
$-(n+1) V_{n+1}$, and therefore
$$\begin{aligned}
&(n+1) V_{n+1}=S\left[A_{n . s}(2 n+1-2 s) r^{2 s-2 n-3} \Sigma\left(p_{m}^{n-2 s+1} \lambda^{s}\right)\right. \\
&\left.-A_{n . s} r^{2 s-2 n-1} \Sigma\left(p^{n-2 s-1} \lambda_{m}^{s+1}\right)\right] .
\end{aligned}$$
(37)
If we wish to obtain the terms containing 8 cosines with
double suffixes, we must diminish $s$ by unity in the last term,
and we find
$$\begin{aligned}
(n+1) V_{n+1}=S\left[r ^ { 2 s - 2 n - 3 } \left\{A_{n . s}(2 n\right.\right. & -2 s+1) \Sigma\left(p_{n}^{n-2 s+1} \Lambda^{s}\right) \\
& \left.-A_{n . s-1} \Sigma\left(p^{n-2 s+1} \lambda_{m}^{s}\right) \dagger\right]
\end{aligned}$$
(38)
Now the two classes of products are not distinguished from
each other in any way except that the suffix $m$ occurs among
the $p$ 's in one and among the $\lambda$ 's in the other. Hence their
coefficients must be the same, and since we ought to be able to
obtain the same result by putting $n+1$ for $n$ in the expression
for $V_{n}$ and multiplying by $n+1$, we obtain the following equa-
tions,
$$(n+1) A_{n+1 \cdot s}=(2 n-28+1) A_{n \cdot s}=-A_{n \cdot s-1} .$$
(39)
If we put $s=0$, we obtain
$$(n+1) A_{n+1 \cdot 0}=(2 n+1) A_{n \cdot 0} ;$$
(40)
and therefore, since $A_{1 \cdot 0}=1$,
$$A_{n, 0}=\frac{2 n!}{2^{n}(n!)^{2}}$$
(41)
and from this we obtain the general value of the coefficient
$$A_{n, s}=(-1)^{\cdot} \frac{(2 n-2 s)!}{2^{n-s} n!(n-s)}$$
